entries.text: A bid is any attempt to connect: a question, a joke, a sigh, a look. Partners turn toward a bid (respond), turn away (ignore it), or turn against it (snap back). Turning toward small bids is the strongest everyday predictor of a relationship lasting. (Gottman)
entries.title: Bids for connection

entries.text: Gottman's four horsemen: criticism ('you always'), contempt (mockery, eye-rolling), defensiveness ('it's not my fault'), stonewalling (shutting down). Contempt is the most corrosive of the four.
entries.title: The four horsemen

entries.text: A repair attempt is any move to de-escalate: an apology, a joke, a touch, 'can we start over?'. Repairs only work if the other person accepts them — accepting a repair matters more than making a perfect one.
entries.title: Repair attempts

entries.text: Perceived responsiveness — feeling understood, validated, and cared for — is what makes a partner feel close. It is built in small moments, not grand gestures.
entries.title: Perceived responsiveness

entries.text: Contempt says 'I am better than you': sarcasm, mockery, name-calling, eye-rolling. It is the single strongest predictor of a relationship ending, and the antidote is describing your own feelings and needs instead of attacking the other person.
entries.title: Contempt

entries.text: Stonewalling is shutting down: one-word answers, silence, leaving the room. It usually means the person is flooded, not that they don't care. The fix is a real break (20+ minutes), then coming back to the conversation.
entries.title: Stonewalling

entries.text: A complaint names a specific problem ('you left the dishes'); criticism attacks character ('you always...' / 'you never...'). Turning a criticism into a complaint — specific, no 'always'/'never' — keeps the conversation solvable.
entries.title: Criticism vs complaint

entries.text: Relationships are built in small moments of turning toward: answering the question, laughing at the joke, noticing the sigh. Most bids are small and easy to miss.
entries.title: Turning toward
